title: The accusative: den, einen, keinen (Der Akkusativ)
summary: The thing an action happens to takes the accusative. Only masculine words change: der becomes den, ein becomes einen, kein becomes keinen.
goals: Use den, einen and keinen after verbs like haben, nehmen and kaufen
Know which words change (only masculine) and which stay the same
Say what there is: es gibt

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 11: Eating and leisure (Lebensmittel)

points: A sentence has a subject (nominative). Many also have an object: the person or thing the action is done to. That object is in the accusative.
Ask [[Wen?]] (whom) for a person and [[Was?]] (what) for a thing: [[Wen liebt Lena?]] - [[Lena liebt einen Mann.]]
Only masculine articles change: [[der]] becomes [[den]], [[ein]] becomes [[einen]], [[kein]] becomes [[keinen]].
Feminine, neuter and plural stay as they are: [[die]], [[das]], [[eine]], [[ein]], [[keine]].
The object can also come first, and the verb stays second: [[Den Apfel esse ich.]]
Compare: [[Das ist ein Apfel.]] (subject, nominative) but [[Ich esse einen Apfel.]] (object, accusative).

phrases.de: Ich kaufe das Kleid. Das Kleid ist elegant.
phrases.en: I'm buying the dress. The dress is elegant.

phrases.de: Hast du einen Bruder? Nein, ich habe keinen Bruder.
phrases.en: Do you have a brother? No, I don't have a brother.

points: The accusative is used in four places. First, the direct object: [[Ich esse einen Apfel.]], [[Ich liebe meine Familie.]]
Second, after the accusative prepositions [[bis]], [[durch]], [[für]], [[gegen]], [[ohne]], [[um]] and [[entlang]]: [[Ich kaufe eine Tasche für meinen Bruder.]]
Third, in time phrases without a preposition: [[jeden Tag]], [[jeden Abend]], [[jede Woche]], [[letzten Sommer]], [[den ganzen Abend]].
Fourth, after most verbs: [[haben]], [[möchten]], [[nehmen]], [[sehen]], [[bestellen]], [[trinken]], [[essen]].
Only masculine changes: [[den]], [[einen]], [[keinen]], and the possessives [[meinen]], [[deinen]], [[seinen]], [[ihren]], [[unseren]], [[euren]], [[Ihren]].
Personal pronouns change too: [[mich]], [[dich]], [[ihn]], [[uns]], [[euch]].

phrases.de: Ich kaufe eine Tasche für meinen Bruder.
phrases.en: I'm buying a bag for my brother.

phrases.de: Ich trinke jeden Tag einen Kaffee.
phrases.en: I drink a coffee every day.

phrases.de: Letzten Sommer war ich in Italien.
phrases.en: Last summer I was in Italy.

notes.extra: Time phrases in the accusative ([[jeden Tag]], [[letzten Sommer]]) and the accusative prepositions.

points: Possessives in the accusative follow [[ein]]: only masculine nouns change, and they add -en: [[Ich liebe meinen Mann.]]
Neuter, feminine and plural stay as they were: [[mein Auto]], [[meine Katze]], [[meine Kinder]].
The masculine forms: [[meinen]], [[deinen]], [[seinen]], [[ihren]], [[unseren]], [[euren]], [[Ihren]].
[[euer]] loses an e: [[euren]], not 'eueren'.
Check with the noun's article: [[der Freund]] gives [[ihren Freund]], but [[die Eltern]] gives [[seine Eltern]].

phrases.en: Do you have your dog with you?

points: Many verbs only make sense with an object in the accusative (transitive verbs): [[Lena trinkt einen Apfelsaft.]] Ask [[Was?]] for a thing and [[Wen?]] for a person.
Verbs from the video: [[trinken]], [[besuchen]], [[vergessen]], [[beantworten]], [[lieben]], [[verstehen]], [[suchen]], [[hören]], [[kennen]], [[sehen]], [[mögen]], [[bauen]], [[stören]] (disturb).
[[beantworten]] takes the accusative ([[Ich beantworte meine E-Mails.]]), but [[antworten]] without be- takes the dative.
[[mögen]] is not only a modal verb: [[Meine Schwester mag Schokolade.]]
These verbs form the Perfekt with [[haben]] (Unit 5).

phrases.en: Lena is drinking an apple juice.

phrases.de: Kennst du die Freundin von Peter?
Ich baue eine Sandburg mit meinen Kindern.
phrases.en: I'm building a sandcastle with my children.

sections.title: Who does it, and what it's done to
sections.text:
In [[Der Mann kauft einen Laptop.]] the man does the buying: he is the subject, in the dictionary form (the nominative). The laptop is what he buys: the object. In German the object takes the **accusative**.

The good news: only **masculine** words show it. [[der]] becomes [[den]], [[ein]] becomes [[einen]], [[kein]] becomes [[keinen]]. Feminine, neuter and plural stay exactly the same.

You've used this since Unit 2 ([[Ich brauche einen Stift.]]) and in lesson 1 ([[Ich möchte einen Kaffee.]]). Here is the whole picture.

sections.title: Which verbs?
sections.text:
Most verbs take an object in the accusative: [[haben]], [[brauchen]], [[möchten]], [[nehmen]], [[kaufen]], [[suchen]], [[finden]], [[bekommen]], [[trinken]] and many more.
- [[Ich nehme den Kuchen.]] = I'll have the cake.
- [[Ich suche den Schlüssel.]] = I'm looking for the key.
- [[Ich finde den Film gut.]] = I think the film is good.
- [[Ich bekomme einen Kaffee.]] = I'll have a coffee. ([[bekommen]] means to get, never 'to become'.)

**Not after [[sein]]:** [[Das ist ein Kaffee.]] [[Das ist der Schlüssel.]] With [[sein]] both sides are the same thing, so nothing changes.

sections.title: es gibt = there is, there are
sections.text:
[[Es gibt]] is followed by the accusative too:
- [[Hier gibt es einen Supermarkt.]] = There's a supermarket here.
- [[Gibt es hier ein Café?]] = Is there a café here?
- [[Heute gibt es keinen Kuchen.]] = There's no cake today.

It's always [[es gibt]], for one thing or many: [[Hier gibt es drei Cafés.]]

Russian has an accusative too (Я беру ручку). Remember the twist from Unit 2: in Russian the feminine changes (ручка becomes ручку) and a masculine thing stays (стол). German is the other way round: [[einen Stift]] changes, [[eine Tasche]] stays.

[[den]] is only for masculine words: [[den Kaffee]], [[den Kuchen]]. Never 'den Milch' or 'den Bier'. So the gender you learn with every noun pays off here: [[der Tisch]] tells you it's [[den Tisch]] and [[einen Tisch]].

items.de: Ich finde den Kuchen sehr gut.
items.en: I think the cake is very good.

items.de: der Kaffee, den Kaffee, einen Kaffee
items.en: the coffee, the coffee (object), a coffee (object)

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I'll have the cake.
items.explanation: der Kuchen is masculine and it's the object: den Kuchen.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I'm buying the milk.
items.explanation: die Milch is feminine: feminine never changes, so die Milch.

items.question: Which sentence means 'I'm looking for a pen'?
items.explanation: der Stift is masculine and the object: einen Stift.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: That's a coffee.
items.explanation: After sein nothing changes: Das ist ein Kaffee.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: There's no café here.
items.explanation: das Café is neuter, so kein stays kein after es gibt.
